title: Tolkien for the unconverted
gist: A cultural notebook by Paul Lay reviewing DJ Taylor's book on JRR Tolkien, a new Covent Garden Parsifal under music director Jakub Hrůša, and Teshigahara's 1964 film Woman in the Dunes. Its main society angle is Tolkien's huge commercial reach (up to 300 million copies) and his status as a near-religious text for tech figures like Elon Musk and Peter Thiel.

insights.claim: JRR Tolkien's works have sold as many as 300 million copies, a scale of commercial success Paul Lay calls astounding.
insights.so_what: It shows how durable and monetisable the Tolkien intellectual property is across books, films and adaptations.
insights.quote: the sheer scale of Tolkien’s commercial success is astounding; as many as 300 million copies sold
insights.locator: Taylor, the acclaimed biographer of Orwell
insights.speaker: Paul Lay

insights.claim: Tolkien, a deeply conservative figure who became a hero of the hippies, now holds near-religious status among tech leaders such as Elon Musk and Peter Thiel.
insights.so_what: Tolkien-derived imagery and values shape Silicon Valley culture and branding, as in company names drawn from Middle-earth.
insights.quote: his oeuvre is now akin to a religious text for tech bros such as Elon Musk and Peter Thiel
insights.locator: Taylor, the acclaimed biographer of Orwell
insights.speaker: Paul Lay

insights.claim: DJ Taylor's The King Under the Mountain is a meditation rather than a biography of Tolkien, and the author speculates the Tolkien estate might not permit a biography.
insights.so_what: Tight estate control over Tolkien material shapes what can be published about him.
insights.quote: Taylor, the acclaimed biographer of Orwell, has not written a biography (would the estate allow it?)
insights.locator: Taylor, the acclaimed biographer of Orwell
insights.speaker: Paul Lay

insights.claim: Paul Lay judges that the Royal Opera's new music director Jakub Hrůša has dispelled doubts about his succeeding Antonio Pappano, based on the orchestra's top form in a new Covent Garden Parsifal.
insights.so_what: A successful handover matters for audiences and funding at a flagship UK cultural institution.
insights.quote: Any doubts raised about his succeeding Antonio Pappano in that role can be swiftly cast aside.
insights.locator: Above all, though, there is the music
insights.speaker: Paul Lay

insights.claim: Hiroshi Teshigahara's 1964 film Woman in the Dunes, adapted from Kōbō Abe's novel, is among Andrei Tarkovsky's top ten films, and the pianist Glenn Gould reportedly saw it over a hundred times and called it a contender for the greatest film ever made.
insights.so_what: Shows the lasting cultural standing of canonical arthouse cinema, though it has little direct investment relevance.
insights.quote: claimed it was a contender for the greatest film ever made
insights.speaker: Paul Lay
